meta.target: consistent improvement to reach high level

weaknesses.name: Throttle hesitation / lift events at corner exit
weaknesses.root_cause_justification: Hesitation / coarse throttle = driver second-guessing. Drill: commit to one throttle application per corner; if it doesn't work, change line, not throttle.

weaknesses.name: Inconsistent peak brake pressure across laps
weaknesses.root_cause_justification: Pedals (Simagic P2000 / hydraulic) already eliminate sensor noise. Inconsistency is in the foot — driver pressure modulation.

weaknesses.name: Coarse throttle application (high jerk)
weaknesses.root_cause_justification: Hesitation / coarse throttle = driver second-guessing. Drill: commit to one throttle application per corner; if it doesn't work, change line, not throttle.

weaknesses.name: Steering input jitter inside corners
weaknesses.root_cause_justification: DD wheel hardware is not the bottleneck — investigate FFB Damping/Smoothing settings and check for FFB clipping in the iRacing Black Box.

weaknesses.name: Brake application rate outside ideal band
weaknesses.root_cause_justification: Slow brake onset = driver not 'stabbing' the pedal at threshold. Drill: practise threshold braking with target peak achieved within 200ms.

weaknesses.name: Mid-corner minimum speed deficit vs. reference lap
weaknesses.cost_math: sum(-Δv × d / v²) across matched corners [PHYSICS-BASED]
weaknesses.root_cause_justification: Mid-corner speed is the sum of entry, line, and trust. Address by working on trail-braking and a later, slower turn-in to carry rotation.

settings.name: Force Feedback Strength
settings.ui_path: Black Box (F9 in-car) > Force Feedback > 'Auto' button
settings.value: Use 'Auto' once per car after 1-2 hot laps; verify the bar is not flashing red
settings.rationale: With a 18 Nm DD wheel, hand-tuning FFB strength risks clipping on high-grip cars. iRacing's Auto sets max torque without clipping, which is the correct ceiling for a DD wheel.
settings.source: iRacing Member Forums — David Tucker FFB documentation

settings.name: Force Feedback Damping
settings.value: 5-10% on DD wheels (start at 5; increase by 1 until jitter quiets)
settings.rationale: Damping suppresses high-frequency oscillations the DD motor amplifies. With Simagic Alpha class hardware, do NOT exceed 10% or the wheel will feel laggy.
settings.source: iRacing Member Guide; Boosted Media FFB Setup Guide

settings.name: Min Force
settings.ui_path: Options > Drive > Force Feedback > Min Force
settings.rationale: DD wheels have no deadzone; Min Force only helps belt/gear wheels.

settings.name: Smoothing
settings.rationale: Smoothing destroys the road texture that DD hardware exists to deliver.

settings.name: Brake Force Factor
settings.ui_path: Options > Drive > Pedals > Brake Force Factor (or Brake Calibration)
settings.value: 1.0 (linear); set max-pressure point so 100% brake = comfortable peak press
settings.rationale: Simagic P2000 reports real pressure. Anything other than linear hides what the pedal is actually doing.

settings.name: Brake Linearity Lookup Table (LUT)
settings.value: Generate a per-driver brake LUT using the iRacing Custom Brake App
settings.rationale: When brake-pressure consistency is the problem on hydraulic pedals, a LUT mapping raw pressure → game-brake response gives the driver a more linear feel and lets them hit the same peak repeatedly.

settings.name: Steering Wheel Range (per car)
settings.ui_path: Options > Drive > Steering Wheel: 'Auto' + verify with car's actual lock
settings.value: Auto — let iRacing match game lock to the car (~480° for Porsche GT3 R)
settings.rationale: Locking the wheel to the car's actual steering range means 1:1 visual feedback. Mid-corner speed deficits often trace to mismatched wheel ratio.

settings.name: Look Ahead / Head Movement
settings.ui_path: Options > Graphics > Driving View > Look Ahead
settings.rationale: Carrying mid-corner speed requires eyes on the exit, not the apex. Increased look-ahead forces the camera to anticipate, which trains the driver's eyes.
settings.source: Coach Dave Academy — Vision and Look-Ahead Training

drills.title: Commit-To-One Throttle
drills.weakness_addressed: Throttle hesitation / lift events at corner exit
drills.description: Force yourself to make ONE throttle application per corner exit — no lifts, no re-applications. If the car oversteers, accept the slide and use it, or pick a different line next lap. The fix is line/entry, not throttle hesitation.
drills.success_criterion: <1 throttle blip per lap on average.

drills.title: Threshold Braking Consistency
drills.weakness_addressed: Inconsistent peak brake pressure across laps
drills.description: Pick one heavy-braking corner. Set a target peak brake pressure (e.g. 85%). Run 15 laps. Goal: hit ±3% of that target every single lap. Do not chase lap time.
drills.success_criterion: Brake peak-pressure CV at the target corner < 0.07 across 10 consecutive laps.

drills.title: Roll-On Throttle Ramp
drills.description: From apex, target a constant rate of throttle increase (e.g. 0 → 100% over 1.5 seconds). Use a metronome app set to ~80 BPM as a mental pacer. The goal is no spikes, no flats.
